fact: The article says the Access to Information Act of 2016 was assented to in February 2017, published in the Gazette on 16 February 2017 and became operational on 30 September 2020, giving a right to information held by public and relevant private bodies.

The article reports that the Malawi Human Rights Commission, which the Act makes its oversight body, issued a notice to the company Mota-Engil to assess whether it had mechanisms to comply with the Act; the High Court on 6 March 2026 found the decision to assess was neither illegal nor unreasonable. The notice itself is undated; the date is the ruling's.
This document is the text of the Access to Information Act, 2016 (Act 13 of 2017), assented to on 10 February 2017, gazetted 16 February 2017 and commenced on 30 September 2020.
The article says the Access to Information Act (ATIA), which gives public access to government-held information, became operational in September 2020.

The Malawi Human Rights Commission, the body Section 8 of the Act gives the oversight role (awareness, advice on information management, review of denials), presented its ATIA implementation progress report on 10 October 2025 (article dated 11 October), so it has taken up the job.

The commission's report for April 2024 to March 2025 says information holders processed over 36,000 requests with 11 rejections; the article is dated 11 October 2025 and the report was presented on the Friday before.
